articleTitle: On Jacquet's conjecture: the split period case
abstract: We complete in the paper our proof of the Jacquet's conjecture for the split period case.

articleTitle: Khintchine-type theorems on manifolds: the convergence case for standard and multiplicative versions
abstract: An analogue of the convergence part of the Khintchine-Groshev theorem, as well as its multiplicative version, is proved for nondegenerate smooth submanifolds in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. The proof combines methods from metric number theory with a new approach involving the geometry of lattices in Euclidean spaces.

articleTitle: On the Hitchin morphism in positive characteristic
abstract: Let X be a smooth projective curve over a field of characteristic p > 0. We show that the Hitchin morphism, which associates to a Higgs bundle its characteristic polynomial, has a nontrivial deformation over the affine line. This deformation is constructed by considering the moduli stack of t-connections on vector bundles on X and an analogue of the p-curvature, and by observing that the associated characteristic polynomial is, in a suitable sense, a p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-power.

articleTitle: G-actions on graphs
abstract: Let G be an n-dimensional torus and let τ be a Hamiltonian action of G on a compact symplectic manifold, M. If M is pre-quantizable, one can associate with τ a representation of G on a virtual vector space, Q(M), by spin<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℂ</sup>-quantization. If M is a symplectic GKM manifold, we show several well-known theorems about this “quantum action” of G: for example, the convexity theorem, the Kostant multiplicity theorem, and the “quantization commutes with reduction” theorem for circle subgroups of G, are basically just theorems about G-actions on graphs.

articleTitle: Twisted GL n loop group orbit and solutions of the WDVV equations
abstract: We show that all (n-component) KP tau-functions, which are related to the twisted loop group of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> n</inf> , give solutions of the Darboux-Egoroff system of PDE's. Using the Geometry of the Grassmannian we construct from the corresponding wave function the deformed flat coordinates of the Egoroff metric and from this the corresponding solution of the Witten–Dijkgraaf–E. Verlinde–H. Verlinde equations.

articleTitle: Dynamical twists in group algebras
abstract: We classify dynamical twists in group algebras of finite groups. Namely, we set up a bijective correspondence between gauge equivalence classes of dynamical twists (which are solutions of a certain nonlinear functional equation) and isomorphism classes of “dynamical data” described in purely group theoretical terms. This generalizes the classification of usual twists obtained by Movshev and Etingof-Gelaki.

articleTitle: Finiteness of simple homotopy types up to s-cobordism of aspherical 4-manifolds
abstract: In this paper we show that for a class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{C}$</tex> of 4-manifolds each member of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{C}$</tex> has only finitely many simple homotopy type up to s-cobordism. This result generalizes a similar result of Hillman for certain complex surfaces. We also present a correction in the proof of Hillman's result.

articleTitle: Pre-Lie algebras and the rooted trees operad
abstract: A pre-Lie algebra is a vector space L endowed with a bilinear product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol\cdot\boldsymbol:\mathbf L\boldsymbol\times\mathbf L\boldsymbol\rightarrow\mathbf L$</tex> satisfying the relation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol(\mathbf x\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf y\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf z\boldsymbol-\mathbf x\boldsymbol\cdot{\boldsymbol(\mathbf y\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf z\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol={\boldsymbol(\mathbf x\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf z\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf y\boldsymbol-\mathbf x\boldsymbol\cdot{\boldsymbol(\mathbf z\boldsymbol\cdot\mathbf y\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol,\textbf{?}\boldsymbol\forall\textbf{?}\mathbf x\boldsymbol,\mathbf y\boldsymbol,\mathbf z\boldsymbol\in\mathbf L$</tex>. We give an explicit combinatorial description in terms of rooted trees of the operad associated to this type of algebras and prove that it is a Koszul operad.

articleTitle: Value distribution for eigenfunctions of desymmetrized quantum maps
abstract: We study the value distribution and extreme values of eigenfunctions for the “quantized cat map.” This is the quantization of a hyperbolic linear map of the torus. In a previous paper it was observed that there are quantum symmetries of the quantum map—a commutative group of unitary operators that commute with the map,which we called “Hecke operators.” The eigenspaces of the quantum map thus admit an orthonormal basis consisting of eigenfunctions of all the Hecke operators, which we call “Hecke eigenfunctions.”In this note we investigate suprema and value distribution of the Hecke eigenfunctions. For prime values of the inverse Planck constant N for which the map is diagonalizable modulo N (the “split primes” for the map), we show that the Hecke eigenfunctions are uniformly bounded and their absolute values (amplitudes) are either constant or have a semi-circle value distribution as N tends to infinity. Moreover, in the latter case different eigenfunctions become statistically independent. We obtain these results via the Riemann hypothesis for curves over a finite field (Weil's theorem) and recent results of N. Katz on exponential sums. For general N we obtain a nontrivial bound on the supremum norm of these Hecke eigenfunctions.

articleTitle: On absolute continuity of the periodic Schrödinger operators
abstract: This paper concerns the Schrödinger operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\Delta+V{(\mathbf x)}$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{R}^d$</tex>, d ≥ 3, with periodic potential V. Under the assumption <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V\in L_\text{loc}^{d/2}{(\mathbb{R}^d)}$</tex>, it is shown that the spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\Delta+V{(\mathbf x)}$</tex> is purely absolutely continuous. The condition on the potential V is optimal in the context of L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> spaces. The proof relies on certain uniform Sobolev inequalities on the d-torus. We also establish the absolute continuity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\Delta+V{(\mathbf x)}$</tex> with certain periodic potential V in the weak- L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d/2</sup> space.

articleTitle: Calabi flow in Riemann surfaces revisited: a new point of view
abstract: In this paper, we observe a set of functionals of metrics which all decrease under the Calabi flow and have uniform lower bound along the flow, which gives rise to a set of integral estimates on the curvature flow. Using these estimates, together with weak compactness we obtained in previous papers [8] and [10], we prove the long-term existence and convergence of the Calabi flow. Thus we give a new proof to Chruscial's theorem. The set of simple ideas of global integral estimates and concentration compactness should have further implications in other heat flow problems.

articleTitle: RC-graphs and a generalized Littlewood-Richardson rule
abstract: Using a generalization of the Schensted insertion algorithm to rc-graphs, we provide a generalization of the Littlewood-Richardson rule for multiplying certain Schubert polynomials by Schur polynomials.

articleTitle: Harmonic functions on manifolds of nonnegative Ricci curvature
abstract: Examples are constructed of noncompact Riemannian manifolds M, having nonnegative Ricci curvature, in each dimension n ≥ 5. These manifolds M support spaces of harmonic functions with subquadratic growth, whose dimension is greater than n + 1, which is the dimension of the corresponding space of harmonic functions on R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>.

articleTitle: The field generated by the points of small prime order on an elliptic curve
abstract: We prove that the field generated by the points of order p of an elliptic curve over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline{\mathbf Q}$</tex> is strictly bigger than the cyclotomic field generated by pth roots of unity,for p 0 a prime number satisfying p = 11 or 17 ≤ p < 1000.

articleTitle: Résonances dans des domaines de taille h
abstract: On travaille dans le cadre de l'analyse semi-classique. On considère un opérateur qui approche −h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Δ à l'infini. Soit E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> > 0 une “valeur régulière” pour P (une valeur non-critique du potentiel dans le cas d'un opérateur de Schrödinger). Sous certaines hypothèses dont celle de l'analycité de P près de l'infini, on montreque le nombre de résonances de P dans des domaines de taille h autour de E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> > 0 est un <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}{\boldsymbol(\mathbf h^{\mathbf1\boldsymbol-\mathbf n}\boldsymbol)}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Endomorphisms of hypersurfaces and other manifolds
abstract: We prove that a smooth hypersurface of degree ≥ 3 in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf P^n{(n\geq3)}$</tex> admits no endomorphism of degree > 1 (for hyperquadrics this is due to Paranjape and Srinivas). We then collect some general results on endomorphisms of projective manifolds. We classify in particular those Del Pezzo surfaces which admit an endomorphism of degree > 1.

articleTitle: Irreducible Tori in semisimple groups
abstract: Let G be an absolutely simple simply connected algebraic group over a global field k. In this note, we analyze arithmetic properties of the maximal k-tori of G .We establish density (in the variety of maximal tori) of the set of maximal k-tori which do not contain proper k-subtori (we call such tori k-irreducible). Using the fact that the k-irreducible tori we construct have the weak approximation property, we extend some of our previous results (contained in Publ. Math. Inst. Haute Etudes Sci. 84 (1996), 91–187, § 9) to global function fields. This allows one to establish the congruence subgroup property for the groups of points of G over semi-local subrings of k. Finally, we examine the strong approximation property in the maximal k-tori of G with respect to generalized arithmetic progressions.Irreducible Tori in semisimple groups (Erratum) dx.doi.org/10.1155/S1073792802112074

articleTitle: Semisimple Frobenius structures at higher genus
abstract: In the context of equivariant Gromov-Witten theory of tori actions with isolated fixed points, we compute genus g > 1 Gromov-Witten potentials and their generalizations with gravitational descendents. Both formulas, with and without descendents, are stated in a form applicable to any semisimple Frobenius structure and therefore can be considered as definitions in the axiomatic context of Frobenius manifolds. In (nonequivariant) Gromov-Witten theory, they become conjectures expressing higher genus GW-invariants in terms of genus 0 GW-invariants of symplectic manifolds with generically semisimple quantum cup-product.

articleTitle: Semi-infinite A-variations of Hodge structure over extended Kähler cone
abstract: In this paper we propose a symplectic analogue of Barannikov's construction of semi-infinite Hodge structure variations over extended moduli spaces of complex structures. It is shown that the duality transformation for mirror torus fibrations over the same Monge-Ampere manifold isomorphically exchanges symplectic semi-infinite A-variations of Hodge structure introduced in this paper with Barannikov's semi-infinite B-variations of Hodge structure.

articleTitle: Mirror symmetry, Langlands duality, and commuting elements of Lie groups
abstract: By normalizing a component of the space of commuting pairs of elements in a reductive Lie group G, and the corresponding space for the Langlands dual group, we construct pairs of hyperkähler orbifolds which satisfy the conditions to be mirror partners in the sense of Strominger, Yau, and Zaslow. The same holds true for commuting quadruples in a compact Lie group. The Hodge numbers of the mirror partners, or more precisely their orbifold E-polynomials, are shown to agree, as predicted by mirror symmetry. These polynomials are explicitly calculated when G is a quotient of SLn.

articleTitle: The Askey-Wilson function transform
abstract: In this paper we present an explicit (rank one) function transform which contains several Jacobi-type function transforms and Hankel-type transforms as degenerate cases. The kernel of the transform, which is given explicitly in terms of basic hypergeometric series, thus generalizes the Jacobi function as well as the Bessel function. The kernel is named the Askey-Wilson function, since it provides an analytical continuation of the Askey-Wilson polynomial in its degree. In this paper we establish the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-theory of the Askey-Wilson function transform, and we explicitly determine its inversion formula.

articleTitle: A remark on the behavior of theta series of degree n under modular transformations
abstract: We prove transformation laws for theta series of degree n attached to integral indefinite quadratic forms. The eighth root of unity with arises under modular transformations is determined explicitly.

articleTitle: Amoebas of Maximal Area
abstract: To any algebraic curve A in (ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> one may associate a closed infinite region A in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> called the amoeba of A. The amoebas of different curves of the same degree come in different shapes and sizes. All amoebas in (ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> have finite area and, furthermore, there is an upper bound on the area in terms of the degree of the curve. The subject of this paper is the curves in (ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> whose amoebas are of the maximal area. We show that up to multiplication by a constant in (ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, such curves are defined over ℝ and, furthermore, that their real loci are isotopic to so-called Harnack curves.

articleTitle: Residual spectrum of odd orthogonal groups
abstract: The purpose of this paper is fourfold. First, we show that the Langlands' functorial lift of a generic cuspidal representation of SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 2n + 1</inf> to GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 2n</inf> is of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{Ind}{\boldsymbol\sigma}_\mathbf1\boldsymbol\otimes\boldsymbol\dots\boldsymbol\otimes{\boldsymbol\sigma}_\mathbf k$</tex>, where σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> i</inf> 's are (unitary) cuspidal representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{GL}}_{\mathbf2{\mathbf n}_\mathbf i}$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol L{\boldsymbol(\mathbf s\boldsymbol,{\mathbf\sigma}_\mathbf i\boldsymbol,\mathbf\Lambda^\mathbf2\boldsymbol)}$</tex>, strengthening the recent result of Cogdell, Kim, Piatetski-Shapiro, and Shahidi. It uses the result of Barbasch and Moy on the spherical unitary dual,and the result of Ginzburg, Rallis, and Soudry that says that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol L{\boldsymbol(\mathbf s\boldsymbol,\mathbf\sigma\boldsymbol\times\mathbf t\boldsymbol)}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol\sigma$</tex> is a cuspidal representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{GL}}_\mathbf m$</tex> and t is a generic cuspidal representation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf2\mathbf n\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}$</tex>, has a pole at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol s\boldsymbol=\mathbf1$</tex>, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol L{\boldsymbol(\mathbf s\boldsymbol,\mathbf\sigma\boldsymbol,\mathbf\Lambda^\mathbf2\boldsymbol)}$</tex> has a pole at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol s\boldsymbol=\mathbf1$</tex>. Second, we give an application of the above result to the problem of determining the residual spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf2\mathbf n\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}$</tex> coming from maximal parabolic subgroups,with the assumption that the completed symmetric square L-function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{GL}}_\mathbf n$</tex> is holomorphic except possibly at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol s\boldsymbol=\mathbf0\boldsymbol,\mathbf1$</tex>. Third, we describe the residual spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_\mathbf5$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{GSp}}_\mathbf4$</tex>, defined over a number field. Even though <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{Sp}}_\mathbf4$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_\mathbf5$</tex> are closely related (isogenous), their residual spectrums are quite different. Fourth, we give a conjectural description of the residual spectrum of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf2\mathbf n\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}$</tex> coming from arbitrary parabolic subgroups, assuming some standard global and local conjectures.

articleTitle: The density of Ramified primes in semisimple p-adic Galois representations
abstract: We show that the set of primes which ramify in a semisimple p-adic representation of the absolute Galois group of a number field is of upper density zero.

articleTitle: On quantum unique ergodicity for Γ ∖ ℍ × ℍ
abstract: The purpose of this note is to point out a connection between the Quantum Unique Ergodicity conjecture of Z. Rudnick and P. Sarnak (or, more precisely, natural higher rank generalizations of this conjecture) and conjectures of H. Furstenberg, A. Katok, and R. Spatzier, and G. Margulis regarding the scarcity of measures invariant under natural ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> actions (d ≥ 2) in the ergodic theory of Lie groups. Our main tool is a new variant of the micro local lift of A. Schnirelman,Y. Colin de Verdière, and S. Zelditch with additional invariance properties. We also sharpen and generalize a related result of Rudnick and Sarnak on scarring of Hecke eigenforms.

articleTitle: Approximate factorization and concentration for characters of symmetric groups
abstract: We prove a factorization-concentration result for characters of symmetric groups. This is then applied to the asymptotic behaviour of the decomposition of the tensor representations. There are connections with the Pastur-Marčenko distribution of random matrix theory, and freely infinitely divisible distributions.

articleTitle: On the fermionic formula and the Kirillov-Reshetikhin conjecture
abstract: The fermionic formula conjectured by Kirillov and Reshetikhin describes the decomposition (as a module for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol U}_\mathbf q{\boldsymbol(\mathbf g\boldsymbol)}$</tex> of a tensor product of multiples of fundamental representations W(mλ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> i</inf> ) of the corresponding quantum affine algebras. In this paper,we show that the conjecture is true for the modules W(mλ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> i</inf> ), if i is such that the corresponding simple root occurs in the highest root of the simple Lie algebra with multiplicity at most 2. In particular, the conjecture is established for all but a few nodes for the exceptional algebras.

articleTitle: On the L2-norm of periodizations of functions
abstract: We prove that the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>([0,1]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> × SO (d)) norm of periodizations of a function from L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>) is equivalent to the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>) norm of the function itself in higher dimensions. We generalize the statement for functions from L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>(ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>) where 1 ≤ p < 2d / (d + 2) in the spirit of the Stein-Tomas theorem.

articleTitle: Sato-Tate equidistribution of Kurlberg-Rudnick sums
abstract: We prove equidistribution results for certain exponential sums that arise in the work of P. Kurlberg and Z. Rudnick on “cat maps.” We show (Theorems 1 and 2) that suitable normalizations of these sums behave like the traces of random matrices in SU (2 ). We also showthat as a suitable parameter varies, the corresponding sums are statistically independent (Theorems 3 and 4). The main tools are Deligne's Equidistribution Theorem, the Feit-ThompsonTheorem, the Goursat-Kolchin-Ribet Theorem, and Laumon's Theorem of Stationary Phase.

articleTitle: Isocategorical groups
abstract: It is well known that if two finite groups have the same symmetric tensor categories of representations over C, then they are isomorphic. We study the following question:When do two finite groups G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 1</inf> , G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 2</inf> have the same tensor categories of representations over C (without regard for the commutativity constraint)? We call two groups with such property isocategorical. We give an example of two groups which are isocategorical but not isomorphic: The affine symplectic group of a vector space over the field of two elements, and an appropriate “affine pseudosymplectic group” introduced by R. Griess (containing the “pseudosymplectic group” of A. Weil). On the other hand, we give a classification of groups isocategorical to a given group. In particular, we show that if G has no nontrivial normal abelian subgroups of order 2 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2m</sup> then any group isocategorical to G must actually be isomorphic to G. The proofs use the theory of triangular Hopf algebras. We also apply the notion of isocategorical groups to study the question: When are two triangular semisimple Hopf algebras isomorphic as Hopf algebras?

articleTitle: Generalized toric arieties for simple nonrational convex polytopes
abstract: We call complex quasifold of dimension k a space that is locally isomorphic to the quotient of an open subset of the space ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> by the holomorphic action of a discrete group; the analogue of a complex torus in this setting is called a complex quasitorus. We associate to each simple polytope, rational or not, a family of complex quasifolds having same dimension as the polytope, each containing a dense open orbit for the action of a suitable complex quasitorus. We show that each of these spaces M is diffeomorphic to one of the symplectic quasifolds defined in [P], and that the induced symplectic structure is compatible with the complex one,thus defining on M the structure of a Kähler quasifold. These spaces may be viewed as a generalization of the toric varieties that are usually associated to those simple convex polytopes that are rational.

articleTitle: Noncomplex smooth 4-manifolds with Lefschetz fibrations
abstract: For every integer g ≥ 2 there exist infinitely many pairwise nonhomeomorphic smooth 4-manifolds admitting genus-g Lefschetz fibration over S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> but not carrying any complex structure. This extends a recent result of Ozbagci and Stipsicz.

articleTitle: Some remarks on a spectral correspondence for maass waveforms
abstract: We prove a detailed result in classical language on a special case of the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{O}^\mathbf1$</tex> be the (cocompact) Fuchsian group consisting of the units of norm one in a maximal order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{O}$</tex> in an indefinite quaternion algebra over ℚ. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf d\boldsymbol=\mathbf d{\boldsymbol(\textbf{O}\boldsymbol)}$</tex> be the discriminant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{O}$</tex>. Our result involves a certain integral transform Θ constructed by Dennis Hejhal (1985). We prove that when chosen appropriately, the map Θ gives a linear bijection between each discrete eigenspace of the Laplacian on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O^{1}\mathscr{H}$</tex> and the space of newforms of the same eigenvalue on the congruence group Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 0</inf> (d). The proof uses trace formulas for the Hecke operators on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{O}^\mathbf1$</tex> and Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 0</inf> (d)

articleTitle: The variety of plane curves with ordinary singularities is not irreducible
abstract: We construct an infinite series of equisingular families of projective plane curves with ordinary multiple points such that each family has irreducible components of different dimensions. This phenomenon has been unknown for curves with ordinary multiple points and disproves some wrong expectations about such curves. We observe also that, for each family, the fundamental groups of the complement of curves in different components coincide (and are abelian). The examples are compared with sufficient irreducibility conditions for equisingular families of plane curves in order to get limits of possible improvements for such sufficient conditions.

articleTitle: On the global regularity of wave maps in the critical Sobolev norm
abstract: We extend the recent result of T. Tao [6] to wave maps defined from the Minkowski space R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>+1, n ≥ 5, to a target manifold N which possesses a “bounded parallelizable” structure. This is the case of Lie groups, homogeneous spaces as well as the hyperbolic spaces H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>. General compact Riemannian manifolds can be imbedded as totally geodesic submanifolds in bounded parallelizable manifolds, see [1], and therefore are also covered, in principle, by our result. Compactness of the target manifold, which seemed to play an important role in [6], turns out however to play no role in our discussion. Our proof follows closely that of [6] and is based, in particular, on its remarkable microlocal gauge renormalization idea.

articleTitle: Mixed-norm estimates for a restricted X-ray transform in ℝ4 and ℝ5
abstract: Let γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> be the curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol\{{\mathbf\gamma}_\mathbf d{\boldsymbol(\mathbf t\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol:{\mathbf\gamma}_\mathbf d{\boldsymbol(\mathbf t\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol={\boldsymbol(\mathbf1\boldsymbol,\mathbf t\boldsymbol,\mathbf t^\mathbf2\boldsymbol,\boldsymbol\dots\boldsymbol,\mathbf t^{\mathbf d\boldsymbol-\mathbf1}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol,\textbf{?}\mathbf t\boldsymbol\in{\boldsymbol\lbrack\boldsymbol-\mathbf1\boldsymbol,\mathbf1\boldsymbol\rbrack}\boldsymbol\}$</tex> in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>. Let l(t,x) denote the line <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol\{\boldsymbol x\boldsymbol+\boldsymbol s{\boldsymbol\gamma}_{\mathbf d{\boldsymbol(\mathbf t\boldsymbol)}}\boldsymbol:\boldsymbol s\boldsymbol\in\mathbb{R}\boldsymbol\}$</tex>. We consider the line complex in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> defined via <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol G}_\mathbf d\boldsymbol={\boldsymbol\{\mathbf l{\boldsymbol(\mathbf t\boldsymbol,\mathbf x\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol:\mathbf t\boldsymbol\in{\boldsymbol\lbrack\boldsymbol-\mathbf1\boldsymbol,\mathbf1\boldsymbol\rbrack}\boldsymbol,\mathbf x\boldsymbol\perp{\mathbf\gamma}_{\mathbf d{\boldsymbol(\mathbf t\boldsymbol)}}\boldsymbol\}}$</tex>. This line complex is a model for a general class called rigid well-curved line complexes. We define the restricted X-ray transform as an operator from functions on ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> to functions on G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> in the following way <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol X\boldsymbol f{\boldsymbol(\mathbf l\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol={\boldsymbol\int}_\mathbf l\boldsymbol f\boldsymbol,\boldsymbol l\boldsymbol\in{\boldsymbol G}_\mathbf d$</tex>.In this paper, we prove almost sharp mixed norm estimates for the restricted X-ray transform in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> and ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>.

articleTitle: A differential analog of a theorem of Chevalley
abstract: In this note a proof of a differential analog of Chevalley's theorem on homomorphism extensions is given. An immediate corollary is a condition of finiteness of extensions of differential algebras and a dozen of equivalent definitions of a differentially closed field, including Kolchin's Nullstellensatz.

articleTitle: On complexes equivalent to $\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 3}$-bundles over $\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 4}$
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 3}$</tex>-bundles over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 4}$</tex> have played an important role in topology and geometry since Milnor showed that the total spaces of such bundles can be exotic spheres. Until recently, there was only one exotic sphere known to admit a metric of nonnegative sectional curvature. In a recent paper, K. Grove and W. Ziller constructed metrics of nonnegative curvature on the total space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 3}$</tex>-bundles over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 4}$</tex>. They also asked for a classification of these bundles up to homotopy equivalence, homeomorphism and diffeomorphism. They also asked the following question: the Berger space, Sp(2)/Sp(1), is a 7-manifold that has the cohomology ring of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 3}$</tex>-bundle over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 4}$</tex>, but does it admit the structure of such a bundle? In this paper we show that any 2-connected, 7-manifold with finite fourth cohomology group is PL-homeomorphic to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 3}$</tex>-bundle over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 4}$</tex> if and only if its linking form is equivalent to a standard form. As a corollary we show that the Berger space has the PL type of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 3}$</tex>- bundle over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 4}$</tex>. We also derive necessary and sufficient conditions for any CW complex to be homotopy equivalent to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 3}$</tex>-bundle over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^{\mathbf 4}$</tex>. One of our results has also been obtained independently by D. Crowley and C. Escher.

articleTitle: Darboux transforms on band matrices, weights, and associated polynomials
abstract: Classically, it is well known that a single weight on a real interval leads to orthogonal polynomials. In Generalized orthogonal polynomials, discrete KP and Riemann-Hilbertproblems, Comm. Math. Phys. 207 (1999), 589–620, we have shown that m-periodic sequences of weights lead to “moments,” polynomials dened by determinants of matrices involving these moments and 2m + 1-step relations between them, thus leading to 2m + 1-band matrices L. Given a Darboux transformations on L, which effect does it have on the m-periodic sequence of weights and on the associated polynomials? These questions will receive a precise answer in this paper. The methods are based on introducing time parameters in the weights, making the band matrix L evolve according to the so-called discrete KP hierarchy. Darboux transformations on that L translate into vertex operators acting on the τ-function.

articleTitle: Quasi-modular forms and trace functions associated to free boson and lattice vertex operator algebras
abstract: We study graded traces of vectors in free bosonic vertex operator algebras and lattice vertex operator algebras. We show in particular that trace functions in these two theories always have the shape <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf f{\boldsymbol(\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol/\mathbf\eta{\boldsymbol(\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}^\mathbf d$</tex> where f(q) is quasi-modular in the case of d free bosons, and modular (i.e., a sum of holomorphic modular forms of various weights) in the case of theories based on a lattice L of rank d. We also show how spherical harmonic polynomials with respect to L are related to primary fields in lattice theories.

articleTitle: Generators for the cohomology ring of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces
abstract: Using the methods developed in [LQW], we obtain a second set of generators for the cohomology ring of the Hilbert scheme of points on an arbitrary smooth projective surface X over the field of complex numbers. These generators have clear and simple geometric as well as algebraic descriptions.

articleTitle: The topological structure of contact and symplectic quotients
abstract: We show that if a Lie group acts properly on a co-oriented contact manifold preserving the contact structure then the contact quotient is topologically a stratified space (in the sense that a neighborhood of a point in the quotient is a product of a disk with a cone on a stratified space). As a corollary we obtain that symplectic quotients for proper Hamiltonian actions are topologically stratified spaces in this strong sense thereby extending and simplifying the results of [SL], [BL].

articleTitle: Global regularity of wave maps, I: small critical Sobolev norm in high dimension
abstract: We show that wave maps from Minkowski space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf R^{\mathbf1\boldsymbol+\mathbf n}$</tex> to a sphere S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> − 1 are globally smooth if the initial data is smooth and has small norm in the critical Sobolev space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{\mathbf H}^{\mathbf n\boldsymbol/\mathbf2}$</tex>, in the high-dimensional case n ≥ 5. A major difficulty, not present in earlier results in this area, is that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{\mathbf H}^{\mathbf n\boldsymbol/\mathbf2}$</tex> norm barely fails to control L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">infty</sup>, potentially causing a logarithmic divergence in the nonlinearity; however, this can be overcome by using co-ordinate frames adapted to the wave map by approximate parallel transport. In the sequel [28] of this paper we address the more interesting two-dimensional case n = 2, which is energy-critical.

articleTitle: Relative Lefschetz action and BPS state counting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a mathematical definition of a new “numerical invariants” of Calabi–Yau 3-folds from stable sheaves of dimension one,which is motivated by the Gopakumar-Vafa conjecture [GV] in M-theory. Moreover, we show that for any projective morphism f : X → Y of normal projective varieties, there exists a natural <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{s}{\boldsymbol\ell}_\mathbf2\boldsymbol\times\textbf{s}{\boldsymbol\ell}_\mathbf2$</tex> action on the intersection cohomology group IH(X,Q) which fits into the perverse Leray spectral sequence.

articleTitle: Elliptic Selberg integrals
abstract: We introduce new Selberg-type multidimensional integrals built of Ruijsenaars' elliptic gamma functions. We show that the vanishing of our integrals for a specific parameter hypersurface implies closed evaluation formulas valid for the full parameter space. The resulting integration formulas contain the Macdonald-Morris constant term identities for nonreduced root systems as special limiting cases.

articleTitle: Le lieu singulier des variétés de Schubert
abstract: On donne une description explicite des composantes irréductibles du lieu singulier d'une variété de Schubert dans une variété de drapeaux classique. Cette description implique une conjecture de Lakshmibai et Sandhya.

articleTitle: Quantum periods, I: semi-infinite variations of Hodge structures
abstract: We introduce a generalization of variations of Hodge structures living over moduli spaces of noncommutative deformations of complex manifolds. Hodge structure associated with a point of such moduli space is an element of Sato type grassmanian of semi-infinite subspaces in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> (X, ℂ) [[ħ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">±1</sup>]]. Periods associated with such semi-infinite Hodge structures enter into mirror symmetry formulas in dimensions greater then three.

articleTitle: Optimal bounds on positive blow-up solutions for a semilinear wave equation
abstract: In this paper, we consider the semilinear wave equation u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> tt</inf> − Δ = u<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup> in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf1\boldsymbol<\boldsymbol p\boldsymbol\leq\mathbf1\boldsymbol+\frac{\mathbf2}{\mathbf N\boldsymbol-\mathbf1}$</tex> and p < 5 if N = 1, p ≠ 3 if N = 2. We prove optimal bounds for positive blow-up solutions u(t, x) of this equation.

articleTitle: A generalization of hall polynomials to ADE case
abstract: Certain computable polynomials are described whose leading coefficients are equal to multiplicities in the tensor product decomposition for representations of a Lie algebra of ADE type.

articleTitle: Toroidal Lie algebras and Bogoyavlensky's (2 + 1)-dimensional equation
abstract: We introduce an extension of the ℓ-reduced KP hierarchy, which we call the ℓ-Bogoyavlensky hierarchy. Bogoyavlensky's 2 + 1-dimensional extension of the KdV equation is the lowest equation of the hierarchy in case of ℓ = 2. We present a group-theoretic characterization of this hierarchy on the basis of the 2-toroidal Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{s}\mathbf\ell_\mathbf\ell^\textbf{tor}$</tex>. This reproduces essentially the same Hirota bilinear equations as those recently introduced by Billig and Iohara et al. We can further derive these Hirota bilinear equations from a Lax formalism of the hierarchy. This Lax formalism also enables us to construct a family of special solutions that generalize the breaking soliton solutions of Bogoyavlensky. These solutions contain the N-soliton solutions, which are usually constructed by use of vertex operators.

articleTitle: A commuting vectorfields approach to Strichartz-type inequalities and applications to quasi-linear wave equations
abstract: We give a new, very different, proof of the recent results of Bahouri and Chemin and Tataru concerning improved well posedness results for quasilinear wave equations. At the heart of such results lies a proof of Strichartz type estimate for solutions to linear wave equations with rough coefficients. Instead of relying on parametrices, we develop a different, geometric mehod of deriving such estimates based on generalized energy estimates and commuting vectorfields.

articleTitle: Néron-Tate projection of algebraic points
abstract: Let X be a geometrically irreducible closed subvariety of an abelian variety A over a number field k such that X generates A. Let V be a finite-dimensional subspace of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf A{\boldsymbol(\overline{\mathbf k}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\otimes\mathbf R$</tex>, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf\pi\boldsymbol:\mathbf A{\boldsymbol(\overline{\mathbf k}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\rightarrow\mathbf V$</tex> be the orthogonal projection relative to a Néron-Tate pairing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\langle,\rangle\boldsymbol:\mathbf A{\boldsymbol(\overline{\mathbf k}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\times\mathbf A{\boldsymbol(\overline{\mathbf k}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\rightarrow\mathbf R$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf V\boldsymbol=\mathbf A{\boldsymbol(\mathbf k\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\otimes\mathbf R$</tex>, we prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf\pi{\boldsymbol(\mathbf X{\boldsymbol(\overline{\mathbf k}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol=\mathbf A{\boldsymbol(\mathbf k\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\otimes\mathbf Q$</tex>, and moreover, there exist <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf c,\mathbf c^{'}>\mathbf 0$</tex> such that for any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf a \in\mathbf A{ (\mathbf k )} \otimes\mathbf Q ,\textbf{?}{ \{\mathbf x \in\mathbf X{ (\overline{\mathbf k} )} :\mathbf\pi{ (\mathbf x )} =\mathbf a\ \mathbf{and}\ \mathbf h{(\mathbf x)}<\mathbf{ch}{(\mathbf a)}+\mathbf c^{'} \}}$</tex>is Zariski dense in X.

articleTitle: The Steinberg relation in $\mathbb{A}^{\boldsymbol-\mathbf1}$-stable homotopy
abstract: We give a short motivic proof of the Steinberg relation in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{A}^{\boldsymbol-\mathbf1}$</tex>-stable homotopy groups overa feld k.

articleTitle: The Dirac operator and conformal compactification
abstract: We give results about the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-kernel and the spectrum of the Dirac operator on a complete Riemannian manifold which is conformally equivalent to the interior of a Riemannian manifold with nonempty boundary.

articleTitle: Bounded length 3 representations of the Virasoro Lie algebra
abstract: We classify the indecomposable bounded length 3 representations of the Virasoro Lie algebra, ν, in which the Casimir operator of the projective subalgebra a of infinitesimal linear fractional transformations acts with distinct eigenvalues. Here the central harge acts trivially, and we find that the variation in the tensor density degrees of the representations in the composition series is usually less than 7, and always less than 9. These cut offs are explained by the a-structure of Λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(ν/a).The technique is to compute the cup products of the 1-cocycles of ν with values in the appropriate spaces of differential operators, which also yields a new proof of a result of Cohen, Manin, and Zagier.

articleTitle: Tangential structures on toric manifolds, and connected sums of polytopes
abstract: We extend work of Davis and Januszkiewicz by considering omnioriented toric manifolds, whose canonical codimension-2 submanifolds are independently oriented. We show that each omniorientation induces a canonical stably complex structure, which is respected by the torus action and so defines an element of an equivariant cobordism ring. As an application, we compute the complex bordism groups and cobordism ring of an arbitrary omnioriented toric manifold. We consider a family of examples B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i,j</inf>, which are toric manifolds over products of simplices, and verify that their natural stably complex structure is induced by an omniorientation. Studying connected sums of products of the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i,j</inf> allows us to deduce that every complex cobordism class of dimension > 2 contains a toric manifold, necessarily connected, and so provides a positive answer to the toric analogue of Hirzebruch's famous question for algebraic varieties. In previous work, we dealt only with disjoint unions, and ignored the relationship between the stably complex structure and the action of the torus. In passing, we introduce a notion of connected sum # for simple n-dimensional polytopes; when P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> is a product of simplices, we describe P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> # Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> by applying an appropriate sequence of pruning operators, or hyperplane cuts, to Q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>.

articleTitle: On formality of some symplectic manifolds
abstract: Let (M, κ) be a compact symplectic manifold of dimension 2n; we prove that, if there exists a κ-calibrated complex structure J such that, with respect to the Hermitian structure g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J</inf>, the Nijenhuis tensor A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J</inf> satisfies, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf0\boldsymbol<\boldsymbol p\boldsymbol<\boldsymbol n\boldsymbol,\textbf{?}{\boldsymbol\Arrowvert\mathbf A\boldsymbol\Arrowvert}\boldsymbol<\boldsymbol K{\boldsymbol(\mathbf n\boldsymbol,\mathbf p\boldsymbol)}\sqrt{{\mathbf\mu}_{\mathbf r\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}{\boldsymbol(\mathbf J\boldsymbol)}}$</tex> (where r = n − p and r (J) is the smallest positive eigenvalue of Δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> J, acting on r + 1-forms), then (M, κ) satisfies the hard Lefschetz condition. Note that this implies that the differentiable Gerstenhaber-Batalin-Vilkovisky algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf\Lambda^{\ast}{(\mathbf M)},\mathbf d^{\star},\mathbf d)$</tex> is integrable (i.e., the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol d\boldsymbol d^{\star}$</tex>-lemma holds). Consequently, the formality of the deRham complexand the existence of a structure of (formal) Frobenius manifold on C [[H <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> (M)]] follow at once; an example shows that the given estimate is sharp.

articleTitle: Global well-posedness below energy space for the 1-dimensional Zakharov system
abstract: The Cauchy problem for the 1-dimensional Zakharov system is shown to be globally well-posed for large data which not necessarily have finite energy. The proof combines the local well-posedness results of Bourgain, Colliander, Ginibre, Tsutsumi, Velo and a general method introduced by Bourgain to prove a similar result for nonlinear Schrödinger equations.

articleTitle: Generic automorphic forms on SO(2n + 1): functorial lift to GL(2n), endoscopy, and base change
abstract: We study the weaklift of generic, automorphic, cuspidal representations of (split) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf2\mathbf n\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}{\boldsymbol(\textbf{A}\boldsymbol)}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{GL}}_{\mathbf2\mathbf n}{\boldsymbol(\textbf{A}\boldsymbol)}$</tex>.We describe its image, showit is injective, and construct the inverse map. This inverse map is constructed by applying certain Gelfand-Graev coef. cients to certain residual Eisenstein series on (split) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf4\mathbf n}{\boldsymbol(\textbf{A}\boldsymbol)}$</tex>. The map is directly related to the structure of Rankin-Selberg integrals (for generic representations) which represent the standard L-functions for SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 2</inf> n + 1 × GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 2n</inf> . We also describe the (generalized) endoscopic weaklift from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf2{\mathbf n}_\mathbf1\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}\boldsymbol\times\boldsymbol\dots\boldsymbol\times{\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf2{\mathbf n}_\mathbf k\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{SO}}_{\mathbf2{\boldsymbol({\mathbf n}_\mathbf1\boldsymbol+\boldsymbol\dots\boldsymbol+{\mathbf n}_\mathbf k\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol+\mathbf1}$</tex>, corresponding to the L-group map from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{Sp}}_{\mathbf2{\mathbf n}_\mathbf1}{(\mathbb{C}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol\times\boldsymbol\dots\boldsymbol\times{\textbf{Sp}}_{\mathbf2{\mathbf n}_\mathbf k}{(\mathbb {C})}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{Sp}}_{\mathbf2{\boldsymbol({\mathbf n}_\mathbf1\boldsymbol+\boldsymbol\dots\boldsymbol+{\mathbf n}_\mathbf k\boldsymbol)}}{\boldsymbol(\mathbb C\boldsymbol)}$</tex>. Finally, we describe a base hange weaklift for generic representations on SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> 2n</inf> + 1, associated to a yclic extension of odd prime degree.

articleTitle: On the local regularity of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili-II equation
abstract: We prove the local well-posedness for the KP-II equation in the anisotropic Sobolev spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf H_{\mathbf x\boldsymbol,\mathbf y}^{{\mathbf s}_\mathbf1\boldsymbol,{\mathbf s}_\mathbf2}{\boldsymbol(\mathbf R^\mathbf2\boldsymbol)}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbf s}_\mathbf1\boldsymbol>\boldsymbol-\mathbf1\boldsymbol/\mathbf3\boldsymbol,\textbf{?}{\mathbf s}_\mathbf2\boldsymbol\geq\mathbf0$</tex>. On the other hand we prove that the crucial bilinear estimate needed for the local well-posedness fails for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbf s}_\mathbf1\boldsymbol>\boldsymbol-\mathbf1\boldsymbol/\mathbf3\boldsymbol,\textbf{?}{\mathbf s}_\mathbf2\boldsymbol=\mathbf0$</tex>.

articleTitle: Almost rational torsion points on semistable elliptic curves
abstract: If P is an algebraic point on a commutative group scheme A/K, then P is almost rational if no two nontrivial Galois conjugates σP, τP of P have sum equal to 2 P. In this paper, we classify almost rational torsion points on semistable elliptic curves over ℚ.
